description: Partial source-extracted accessibility examples, not complete article coverage. No authorized source or compatibility review performed. Source excerpts retain identifiers/grouping and are normalized for whitespace. Objective/functional statement_text stores the printed pair, not an invented definition.

documents.edition: 2023 Alberta Edition, second printing (April 2026 revisions and errata)

attributions.statement_text: Intent 1. To limit the probability that persons using a wheelchair or other assistive mobility device will have difficulty using a ramp without the assistance of another person.

attributions.statement_text: Intent 1. To limit the probability that persons using a wheelchair or other assistive mobility device will be unable to control the movement of the wheelchair or device, which could lead to harm to the person or persons nearby.

attributions.statement_text: Intent 1. To limit the probability that persons using a wheelchair or other assistive mobility device will not be able to be served at a service counter or to use a work surface or counter independently.

attributions.statement_text: Intent 1. To limit the probability that a wheelchair or other assistive mobility device used by a person will be trapped in a walking surface, which could lead to the loss of balance of the person, which could lead to harm to the person or persons nearby.

attributions.statement_text: Intent 1. To limit the probability that a wheelchair or other assistive mobility device used by a person will be trapped in a walking surface, which could impede the person's ability to circulate.

attributions.statement_text: Intent 1. To exempt doorways from the minimum width requirements stated in Sentence 3.8.3.2.(1) and permit a lesser minimum width, on the basis that doorways comprise a small portion of a pathway. This is to limit the probability that persons using a wheelchair or other assistive mobility device will not be able to circulate within a building independently.
